item.title: Fenland residents invited to share views on dog control rules
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Fenland residents invited to share views on dog control rules
Fenland District Council is seeking public feedback on proposals to extend dog control regulations across the region. The current Public Spaces Protection Order, which mandates rules such as keeping dogs on leads in cemeteries and fenced play areas, is due to expire this December.
The consultation, which began on September 11, asks residents for their views on extending these measures for another three years until December 2029, alongside potential minor adjustments. You have until October 9 to submit your response. Feedback will be presented to cabinet members in November to help decide whether to extend, amend, or end the order. Full details are available on the Fenland District Council website.
🔗 More details: https://www.fenlandcitizen.co.uk/news/share-your-views-on-dogs-in-public-spaces-9485340/

item.title: Over 10,000 sign petition to support Queen Elizabeth Hospital
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Over 10,000 sign petition to support Queen Elizabeth Hospital
A campaign to protect vital services at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn has reached a significant milestone, with more than 10,000 people signing a petition. Liberal Democrat Rob Colwell, who is leading the initiative, thanked the public for their support in safeguarding local emergency and hospital care.
Supporters are now being invited to take part in a demonstration at the Tuesday Market Place on October 17. Participants are asked to gather at 11:30 am for a "Human A&E queue" event. Attendees are encouraged to bring a sign displaying their home town or village and their travel time to the hospital, as the QEH Community Action Group prepares to submit the petition.

Residents in Wisbech are invited to attend a Volunteer and Community Fair taking place next month. The free event will be held at the Queen Mary Centre on Queens Road on Saturday, November 14, between 10am and 1pm.

Plans unveiled for £13 million King’s Lynn development
Proposals have been revealed for a new £13 million retail development near the Jubilee roundabout in King’s Lynn. Developer Rothstone is working on plans for a site south of Beveridge Way, which would feature an Aldi supermarket, an EG petrol station, and a Starbucks drive-thru. The project is expected to create up to 80 full and part-time jobs.
A public consultation on the scheme is now open and will run until Monday, October 12. Residents can share their views on the proposals online, by phone, or by post before a formal planning application is submitted. Further details on how to provide feedback are available through the project’s consultation team.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Protest planned in Leverington over asylum seeker hostel proposal
A peaceful protest is scheduled for this Sunday in Leverington regarding government plans to use Roman Court as a hostel for asylum seekers. Organised by Reform county councillor Chris Tirrell, the gathering will begin at noon at Troughton Way. The proposal aims to house 26 women and children at the site, as part of a wider plan to accommodate 205 asylum seekers across the Fenland district.
Both the local district council and MP Steve Barclay have expressed opposition to the move. A final decision on the future of the Roman Court site is expected from the government by October 16.

item.title: Police appeal for witnesses following King's Lynn collision
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Police appeal for witnesses following King's Lynn collision
Police are appealing for information following a collision at the Southgates roundabout in King's Lynn last Thursday morning. The incident occurred shortly before 6:30am and involved a white BMW and a motorbike. The motorcyclist was taken to the Queen Elizabeth Hospital with a broken wrist and ankle injuries.
A man in his 40s was arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by dangerous driving and driving while disqualified. He has been released on bail until November 24 while investigations continue. Officers are asking anyone with dashcam footage from the area at the time of the collision to come forward.

New craft hub to open on King’s Lynn High Street this weekend
A new craft hub, Pia’s Place, is set to open on King’s Lynn High Street this weekend. Owned by Gaywood resident Pia Cawston, the shop will offer a variety of creative workshops, including basket weaving, watercolour painting, and children’s activities. The venue also features a selection of vintage items alongside coffee and homemade cake.
The doors open to the public this Saturday from 9am until 3pm, and Sunday from 10am until 4pm. Following the launch, the shop will operate from Wednesday to Sunday, between 9am and 4pm. The owner describes the new venture as a space for all ages to enjoy.

Four council-run leisure centres in West Norfolk have been awarded a ‘very good’ rating following a national quality assessment. The sites, managed by Alive West Norfolk, include Lynnsport and St James’ Pool in King’s Lynn, Downham Leisure, and The Oasis in Hunstanton.
The Quest for Facilities scheme evaluated the centres through mystery visits and independent inspections, focusing on areas such as customer service, safety, and community engagement. Council officials have praised the staff for their ongoing commitment to maintaining high standards across all four facilities.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Norwich Road in Wisbech to close for gas pipe replacement
Drivers in Wisbech are being warned of a lengthy road closure starting next month. Norwich Road will be shut to all vehicles between Churchill Road and Bowthorpe Road from October 5 until December 18. Cadent Gas Ltd is carrying out the work to replace old pipes with new plastic infrastructure.
While the road will be closed to through traffic, access to local properties will be maintained. A diversion route will be in operation throughout the works. The company says some residents may experience temporary gas supply interruptions and that site teams will provide further information to those affected.
